## Read this first: I killed processes I was not allowed to touch

While reproducing the daemon bug, my repro script had a quoting bug. Inside the function I called `count $2`, so the function's `$2` was empty and the process filter became `*` + `*daemon start*`. Its cleanup loop then ran `taskkill /F` on 18 `node ... daemon start --foreground` processes across the whole machine, not just my temp workspace. That broke the "do not kill existing processes" rule.

- **PIDs killed:** 40260 30304 47792 29620 43688 23452 48496 42332 41132 29972 41948 34708 16276 26440 55204 48988 39696 22936.
- **What they were:**
  - 41948, 34708 and 16276 were the ruflo-smoke daemons you reported.
  - 55204 and 48988 were idle duplicates from my own earlier repro.
  - The rest were most likely the "open source project" (5) and freight-recovery (2) daemons, plus my temp-workspace ones. I can't confirm this; the processes are gone.
- **Impact:**
  - Only ruflo background worker daemons were affected; they restart on the next CLI use.
  - Their cleanup handlers never ran, so their `daemon.pid` files are stale. Auto-start treats a dead PID as stale and recovers.
  - Any worker that was mid-run in those daemons was cut off.
- **Now:** the filter is fixed and checked (it matches nothing for an unknown workspace). All killing is removed from the script, and nothing else was killed after that.
- **Machine state:** only 2 `daemon start` processes remained machine-wide at the time I checked.

## Branch
`fix/core-session-paths` in worktree `C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-core-bugs`. Nothing pushed.
```
f8a1f8408 fix(daemon): stop duplicate/zombie daemons per workspace (win32)
72c6228e1 fix(claims): resolve user-level claims.json via os.homedir() on Windows
966d8a064 fix(mcp): start the MCP server in the session project, fix win32 home guard
```
I added `shared`, `swarm` and `security` under `v3/@claude-flow` to the sparse set so vitest could load the sources.

## Fix 1: the MCP server used the wrong project folder (the known bug)
- **Bug:** `mcp-launch.cjs` started `mcp start` in its own cwd and never looked at the session's project. Also, `getProjectCwd()` only treated `'/'` and `$HOME` as "no project". On Windows `HOME` is usually unset and the root is `C:\`, so neither check ever matched.
- **Before:**
  - node:test `server cwd ...\mcp-launch-session-2Jz7a6 should be project ...\mcp-launch-project-OORaO8`; the `resolveProjectDir` test also failed.
  - vitest 3 of 5 failed, e.g. `expected 'C:\Users\mariu' to be '<cwd>'`, `'C:\USERS\MARIU\'`, `'C:\'`.
- **Change:**
  - `plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/mcp-launch.cjs`:
    - Resolves the project folder: `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` first, then `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD`, then the launcher cwd. Home, root and missing folders are skipped.
    - Starts the server in that folder with `CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD` set, so tools that read raw `process.cwd()` (memory, hooks, browser) also agree.
    - Looks for a local CLI install from the project folder.
    - Prints a warning on stderr when there is no project.
  - `v3/@claude-flow/cli-core/src/mcp-tools/types.ts`: new `isNonProjectDir` treats any filesystem root, or the home folder (`os.homedir()`, `HOME` or `USERPROFILE`; case- and trailing-slash-insensitive on win32), as no project.
  - Tests: additions to `plugins/ruflo-core/scripts/mcp-launch.test.cjs` and a new `v3/@claude-flow/cli-core/__tests__/project-cwd-home-guard.test.ts`.
- **After:** node:test 13/13 pass, vitest 5/5 pass.
- **Unverified:**
  - I could not confirm that Claude Code passes `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` to MCP servers. It is not set in this session's Bash environment.
  - No MCP process can follow an in-session `cd`. In your neural-mesh case the session started in `C:\Users\mariu`, so the server will now warn instead of silently using home, but it still can't find neural-mesh by itself.
  - Behaviour change: a relative `RUFLO_MCP_CLI_OVERRIDE` now resolves from the project folder, not the launcher cwd.

## Fix 2: `claims check` ignored the user-level policy on Windows
- **Bug:** `resolve(process.env.HOME || '~', ...)` became `<cwd>\~\.config\claude-flow\claims.json` when `HOME` was unset, so `%USERPROFILE%\.config\claude-flow\claims.json` was never read.
- **Before:** `expected { success: false } to match object { success: true }`.
- **Change:** `v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/commands/claims.ts` now uses `os.homedir()`, and both lookups share `getClaimsConfigPaths()`. Test: `cli/__tests__/claims-user-config-home-win32.test.ts`.
- **After:** 1/1 pass.

## Fix 3: duplicate and zombie daemons per workspace (your report)
- **Root causes:**
  1. When the launcher lock was busy, waiters gave up after a fixed 5s, deleted the lock and carried on without it. On Windows the lock holder runs `tasklist /v`, which often takes longer than 5s, so every waiter forked its own daemon.
  2. A forked `--foreground` child whose `WorkerDaemon.start()` declined (another live daemon owns `daemon.pid`) still parked forever on a keep-alive interval: no workers, no TTL. On exit it would also delete the other daemon's PID file.
- **Before:**
  - With installed ruflo 3.56.3, three concurrent `memory retrieve` in a fresh project left 3 `daemon start --foreground` processes (25676, 55204, 48988); `daemon.pid` named only 25676.
  - New vitest 2/2 failed: one timed out (the zombie child parks forever), the other showed the live holder's lock was deleted.
- **Change:**
  - `cli/src/commands/daemon.ts`:
    - A lock is only taken over, atomically, when its holder PID is dead. While the holder is alive, waiters wait (`RUFLO_DAEMON_LOCK_WAIT_MS`, default 60s) and then decline.
    - A declined foreground child returns instead of parking.
    - The exit cleanup only removes a PID file that holds its own PID.
  - Test: `cli/__tests__/daemon-singleton-win32-zombies.test.ts`.
- **After:**
  - vitest 2/2 pass; the existing `daemon-lockfile-race-2484` test still passes.
  - End to end, on a sandbox copy of the installed 3.56.3 with the same patch applied to its built JS: one daemon per workspace on two runs (17712, 28564), and `daemon stop` left 0. The global install was not touched.
- **Unverified:** I could not build the TypeScript CLI here, so the end-to-end check ran on the patched 3.56.3 JS, not on the built source.

## Re-running the tests
- **Launcher:** `cd plugins/ruflo-core/scripts && node --test mcp-launch.test.cjs`
- **vitest:** I used vitest 4 installed in the scratchpad, symlinked as `node_modules` inside cli and cli-core (symlinks now removed).
  - I needed a scratch config with `oxc: { tsconfig: false }` plus aliases for `@claude-flow/security` and `@claude-flow/cli-core`. Without it, `cli/__tests__` files fail on missing sparse tsconfig references.
  - Command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config <scratch>/cli.vitest.config.mjs __tests__/<file>`, with the same pattern for cli-core.
  - In a full checkout, plain `npx vitest run <file>` should work but is unverified.

## Findings not fixed
1. **Medium:** `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts:206` and `:280` use `process.env.HOME`. On Windows, `~/.claude/settings.json` (stale-npx check) and `~/.claude/helpers` (helper integrity check) are never checked. Found by reading the code; no test written.
2. **Medium:** `cli/src/transfer/storage/gcs.ts:139` and `:207` use `TMPDIR || '/tmp'`, which becomes `C:\tmp` on Windows, and `execFileSync('gcloud')` without shell can't launch `gcloud.cmd`. Found by reading the code.
3. **Medium, from evidence:**
   - What happens: `resolveDaemonProjectRoot` walks up to `C:\Users\mariu`, which has `claude-flow.config.json` and `.swarm`. Every non-git folder under home therefore gets the home folder's daemon.
   - The proof: 4 existing tests in `daemon-autostart.test.ts` fail on this machine, both with and without my change.
   - It also bypasses Fix 1's home guard on the daemon side.
4. **Low:** a fifth test, in `daemon-workspace-scope.test.ts`, hardcodes POSIX paths and fails on win32 (`expected 'C:\Users\me\proj-a' to be '/Users/me/proj-a'`), unrelated to my change.
5. **Medium:** `killStaleDaemons` and `scanRunningDaemons` (`daemon.ts`, around line 1000) use `tasklist /v`, which shows window titles, not command lines. Matching by workspace likely never works on Windows, so stale-daemon cleanup is ineffective there. Inferred from the code, not tested.
